commits.title: Esc in a text prompt no longer closes the book
commits.details:
Cancelling a prompt with Esc inside a book also closed the book and sent
the writer back to the shelf. That happens with Rename tab (double-click
Notes or Outline), File > Email Settings (also asked the first time a
draft is emailed), and Format > Body Font > Other Font. The prompt
removes itself before the key bubbles up, so the editor's own Esc found
nothing open and closed the book. Both prompts now keep their Esc to
themselves, as the choice dialogs and menus already do.

commits.title: The shortcuts window shows the Vim keys section
commits.details:
With View > Vim Keys on, the shortcuts window was meant to list the vim
keys in a section of their own, but the window places its sections in
two columns by number, and the new section's number was in neither, so
it never appeared. It now runs across both columns below them, its rows
in two columns of their own. In either column alone it would have made
that column twice as long as the other.

commits.title: Vim keys work on every keyboard layout
commits.details:
With View > Vim Keys on, a keyboard that types another alphabet left the
writer stuck after Esc. On a Russian, Ukrainian, Bulgarian or Greek
layout every letter key prints Cyrillic or Greek, which moving mode
ignored, so not even i or a went back to writing. Neither Esc nor a
click helped; only switching the system to an English layout, or turning
Vim Keys off, did. Moving keys now count by where they sit on the
keyboard, named as on a US one. The key under the right index finger is
j on every layout, Shift+4 is $, and Ctrl+D and Ctrl+U work there too.

Moving, nothing a keyboard types lands in the text any more. On layouts
with dead keys (German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch, US
International, Greek), a dead key and then a letter put the accented
letter into the chapter: ^ then e typed ê. On Windows and a Mac, a
character typed with AltGr or Option did the same. A dead key now counts
by its place like any other key, and what it composes is taken back
out; AltGr and Option characters are refused.

One change for Latin layouts whose letters sit elsewhere. On French
AZERTY or German QWERTZ, keys went by their printed label and now go by
their place, as on every other layout. Word forward is the key where w
sits on a US keyboard, which AZERTY labels Z, and digits for counts
need no Shift on AZERTY. Writing is unchanged.

commits.title: Word counts no longer lose a word at every paragraph break
commits.details:
From #198: a 5,010-word manuscript of 430 paragraphs showed 4,581 words. Chapter text was read with innerText from a copy of the chapter that is never on screen, and off screen innerText is plain textContent: the paragraphs run together, so "end.

Next" was one word. The page counter read the text before the caret with a range's toString, which does the same. - chapterText puts a line after each paragraph, so the book and chapter counters, today's words, sprints, the page counter, the shelf's goal bar, the cover-painting threshold and the email draft's subject count every word. So does the page counter for the text before the caret. - The cover painter and a deleted chapter's Darlings preview get the paragraphs on lines of their own instead of run together. - A book opened earlier on the day of the update shows the words it gains as written today. The next day counts true. - The SHA-256 fingerprint in an emailed draft is taken from this text, so a manuscript's fingerprint changes once with this update. - npm run test:words: a book imported as a dropped file is, its counts read off the screen.

commits.title: A double-clicked word shows "1 selected"
commits.details:
The double click's first click moves the caret, and a moved caret asks
for a recount 150 ms later. The word the second click selected got its
count, and then the recount put the book's total back over it. Any
change of selection now calls off a recount still waiting.

commits.title: A power cut no longer takes a book off its shelf (#219)
commits.details:
book.json is rewritten every few seconds while a book is open. The new
file was swapped in before its words reached the disk, so a power cut at
that moment could leave the swap done and the file empty; an unreadable
book.json drops the book from the shelf. Chapters, notes and the outline
were written in place, with the same exposure.

- Every library write: a .tmp beside the file, fsync, then the swap.
- JSON files keep their last whole version as .bak; a read that finds the
  file unreadable takes the .tmp, then the .bak, and puts it back.
- A book.json lost with no copy is rebuilt from the chapter files, titled
  from _catalog.txt; a lost library.json puts every book on one shelf.
- scripts/power-loss.test.js leaves files the way a cut write can (empty,
  half-written, gone) and checks the book is still there. The old code
  fails five of its seven tests.

commits.title: npm run bundle and npm run release: one line each for Hugh's two routines
commits.details:
- npm run bundle: takes the newest .bundle in Downloads (or one named),
  checks it fits, merges it into main and pushes. Says so plainly and
  changes nothing when it doesn't fit, when it's already in, or when
  there are uncommitted edits.
- npm run release: sets the next patch version (or the one given) in
  package.json and package-lock.json, commits, pushes main and the tag,
  and prints the commits since the last release as a start on the notes.
  Finishes a release that stopped halfway instead of skipping a number;
  refuses a version that isn't newer or a tag that already exists.
- AGENTS.md tells future sessions to hand Hugh these, not raw git.

commits.title: A library Documents can't hold goes beside it; "Start writing" says why it can't save (#244)
commits.details:
On Windows, a Documents folder redirected to a OneDrive path that isn't
set up on the computer refuses every write (ENOENT). NEO's launch check

commits.title: Undo: outline changes come back with ⌘Z, hints stay hints, typing is taken back by the pause (#241)
commits.details:
- ⌘Z in the outline undoes a line added, removed, or turned into a chapter
  or a section (Enter, Tab, Shift+Tab, Backspace, Delete section). Typing in
  a line is still undone first, by the engine; the caret returns to the line
  the writer was on.
- Shift+Tab on a section now takes the sections after it along, so the
  plan keeps its order (B in A B C: B and C become the next chapter, A
  stays). Sections the writer has already written over stay where their
  prose is.
- Undoing a deletion in the manuscript no longer turns the last gray outline
  hint into real text: undo and redo don't count as writing over a hint, and
  the hint returns with its words.
- ⌘Z took back one letter at a time because the bottom-bar counters
  replaced their text node on every keystroke, which ends the engine's undo
  run. They now change the text in place, and a second's pause ends a run, so
  an undo takes back a burst of typing, not a letter and not a page.

commits.title: Outline cards: the outline as index cards, set like a page; the note walks ahead
commits.details:
The Outline tab lays the book out as index cards that read left to right,
line after line: a chapter starts at its numeral and its sections share a
mat, rounded where the chapter starts and ends, cut square where it wraps.
Parts start a fresh line. Cards come from the manuscript itself, so every
*** section is a card, outlined or not, showing its first line until it has
a note. Click a card to write on it; Enter makes the next card, and Enter on
an empty one a new chapter. Dragging a card (mouse or a held finger) moves
the writing with it; ⌘Z puts it back. Right-click to make a section a
chapter or go to it on the page. Loose cards wait in the right-hand pane
while the Outline is up. ⌘− and ⌘+ size the cards, down to tiles. The list
stays one click away; scripts keep it.

Writing over a gray ghost no longer loses the note: it rides one line below
the paragraph being written, never saved, with a faint Dismiss.

syncGhosts now leaves a ghost where it stands instead of moving every ghost
to the end of its chapter.

commits.title: Outline cards for scripts: every scene a card

heading, its length in eighths, who's in it, and a note (or its first line

Drag a card to move the scene; a loose card dropped on the board becomes a
new scene. Notes live in book.sceneNotes, keyed by an id on the heading.

commits.title: Outline cards: Enter finishes a card, Tab goes to the next; + makes new cards
commits.details:
Enter used to start a new card, so a few stray presses made blank cards and
chapters. Now Enter puts the card down; Tab and ⇧Tab move through the cards
that are there; ⌥Enter (Alt+Enter) makes a new one. A + on the seam after
each card (on hover) adds a card there, a New card button sits on an open
card, and a dashed + Chapter (+ Scene in a script) ends the board. An open
card keeps the section's first line in view above the note, so opening it
never looks like it wiped the card.

commits.title: Outline: Enter makes chapters, Tab makes sections; drop a chapter on a chapter; brighter outside the manuscript
commits.details:
In the List, Enter always makes a new chapter (after the whole chapter,
from a section's line) and Tab always makes a section: a section's line
starts a new one below; a chapter's line becomes a section of the chapter
above, writing and all. ⇧Tab still makes a section a chapter again.

On the cards, a chapter dropped on the middle of another chapter's card
becomes its section (the card lights up and says so); a section dropped
there goes to that chapter's end. Both use joinChapter: the lines move,
the receiving chapter is saved, and only then is the empty one removed.
⌘Z puts it back.

Brighter Interface is now remembered twice: while writing (faint unless
chosen) and on the Outline, Notes and Darlings (bright unless turned
down). The View menu changes the one for the tab you're on.
